Continuous aim error is the world-space angular error in degrees between the zero-corrected bore ray and the muzzle-to-target ray.
ELTS build plan and architecture specification
A target's canonical position is world-space; screen coordinates are derived each frame and never canonical target state.
ELTS build plan and architecture specification
Unity sends head pose, target coordinates, turret angles, or individual LED commands to ELTS; only lifecycle commands are allowed.
ELTS build plan and architecture specification
The study uses no HMD and nothing near the eyes beyond approved measurement equipment.
ELTS build plan and architecture specification
All application timestamps derive from one monotonic clock started at application launch; UTC is only an alignment anchor.
ELTS build plan and architecture specification
Every tracking sample contains connection and validity flags; invalid poses are excluded and never interpolated.
ELTS build plan and architecture specification
Trackers bind by configured serial number, never device index.
ELTS build plan and architecture specification
Logged tracking uses zero prediction; rendering-only head prediction is isolated and the weapon pose remains raw.
ELTS build plan and architecture specification
Trigger handling accepts the first falling edge and applies the configured lockout, nominally 20 ms.
ELTS build plan and architecture specification
The primary block DV remains the count of TargetDestroyed events during the fixed 300-second block.
ELTS build plan and architecture specification
Scenario, behavior, scoring, session, geometry, display, and ELTS transport choices remain data-driven or interface-driven.
ELTS build plan and architecture specification
Participant and operator rendering remain independent; operator content never reaches the participant display.
ELTS build plan and architecture specification
Heartbeat timeout, maximum on-time, and normally closed physical E-stop operate as independent safeguards.
ELTS build plan and architecture specification
Software overrides or weakens the physical E-stop.
ELTS build plan and architecture specification
Safety-critical ELTS changes receive human review and repeat the applicable fail-safe and bench tests.
ELTS build plan and architecture specification
The LED exposure basis and operational limits are documented and agree with software guards.
ELTS build plan and architecture specification
The mock weapon is inert, visibly marked, secured, and covered by campus notification procedures.
ELTS build plan and architecture specification
A failed daily registration check stops participant operation until recalibration and incident recording are complete.
ELTS build plan and architecture specification
Committed code or configuration contains user-specific absolute paths.
Release scripts and runtime work from arbitrary writable extraction paths, including paths with spaces.
Bootstrap and first-run operations are idempotent.
Provisioning backs up existing local configuration or calibration before replacement.
The study runtime requires the Unity Editor.
Prepared study operation requires internet connectivity.
Diagnostics emit both readable output and a versioned machine-readable report.
A new physical rig receives a new rig identity and required recalibration instead of inheriting old calibration silently.
Unbundled prerequisites are precisely documented and detected.
Every study release is verified after copy and extraction, not only in the build directory.
Every configuration type has a versioned JSON Schema.
Unknown, missing, or mistyped required fields cause a precise startup failure.
Every effective configuration file is hashed and recorded in logs and build provenance.
local.json is generated from a committed example and contains only whitelisted machine-local fields.
local configuration, participant calibration, participant data, credentials, or machine secrets are committed.
Study settings and machine-local settings are mixed in one layer.
A schema change increments a version and provides a migration or declares incompatibility.
Configuration precedence is deterministic and documented.
The operator can inspect effective configuration and hashes before a session.
A frozen study configuration change during data collection creates a new tag and study-log entry.
The system uses one monorepo for Unity, Jetson, analysis, config, tooling, documentation, and governance.
Root config is the sole hand-edited source; Unity StreamingAssets receives a generated staged copy.
Git submodules are used before study-v1.0.
Vendored OpenVR files include upstream version, license, and checksums.
Unity ProjectSettings, package manifests, lockfiles, and all .meta files are committed.
Unity Library, Temp, Logs, obj, Build, Builds, or UserSettings directories are committed.
Binary baseline artifacts also receive diffable normalized exports for agents and review.
Repository paths and scripts use portable relative resolution from the repository or release root.
The exact Unity 6 LTS editor version is pinned and checked.
Unity and Python dependencies are locked with committed lockfiles.
Study releases are built from a clean Git worktree.
Dirty development builds identify themselves and cannot be used for participant data collection.
The build records tag, commit, versions, schemas, configuration hashes, target, UTC, and artifact checksum.
The release contains FIRST-RUN, CHECK-SYSTEM, START-ELTS, operator docs, licenses, build-info, and MANIFEST.sha256.
CI specifies an explicit Unity build target or profile for reliable command-line builds.
Reproducibility claims are functional and provenance-based unless bit-for-bit determinism is separately proven.
main represents coherent, tested, documented work.
Normal changes reach main through a pull request and required checks.
One task maps to one temporary branch and one active owner.
Pull requests use squash merge and merged branches are deleted.
The same task branch is edited simultaneously on multiple machines.
A conflict is resolved deliberately and all affected checks are rerun.
Force pushes or deletion of main are allowed.
Safety, invariants, frozen configuration, and study release tags receive human approval.
An agent reads the canonical instruction chain before editing.
An agent inspects PROJECT_STATE.json and its assigned atomic-step row before work.
An agent declares task, branch, owner, scope, claimed paths, and stop conditions.
An agent changes unrelated files merely to clean up the repository.
An agent invents values for unresolved D-01 through D-18 decisions.
An invariant or authority conflict becomes a recorded blocker for human resolution.
Agents preserve user changes and avoid destructive Git operations.
Interface, schema, configuration, or observable behavior changes update tests and documentation in the same pull request.
Work is marked done without required evidence.
Agents record commands and checks run, results, and evidence paths.
An agent merges or releases its own work without required human authority.
Two agents own the same task or branch concurrently.
Parallel agents use separate worktrees and non-overlapping module scopes.
A handoff records completed work, remaining work, changed files, tests, risks, blockers, and next eligible step.
Trello and GitHub Issues are coordination mirrors; repository plan, events, evidence, and decisions remain canonical.
The immutable workbook is normalized into a versioned task catalog with stable IDs.
Progress changes are append-only events with unique IDs and actor, time, branch, transition, and evidence fields.
PROJECT_STATE.json is generated deterministically from the task catalog and events.
Agents hand-edit generated PROJECT_STATE.json after the reducer exists.
Task transitions follow the documented state machine and invalid transitions fail.
G0 through G8 are hard gates and require explicit evidence-backed pass events.
Completing tasks automatically passes a gate.
The current step is chosen deterministically from active, verification-pending, ready, or blocked work in sequence order.
Divergent event chains for one task fail reduction and require reconciliation.
Done or passed states carry evidence that can be resolved in Git, CI, or approved lab records.
The generated state records source artifact hashes, plan version, event count, and generation time.
If all eligible work is blocked, state mode is blocked and lists exact blocker IDs.
AGENTS.md is the canonical model-agnostic instruction entry point.
Model-specific instruction files are thin adapters and do not duplicate policy.
Each module contract states purpose, boundaries, interfaces, thread ownership, schemas, config, events, failure behavior, tests, invariants, ADRs, and work-item links.
Architecture decisions use immutable ADR history with Proposed, Accepted, Rejected, or Superseded status.
D-01 through D-18 are renumbered or replaced by ADR identifiers.
Documentation changes occur in the same pull request as the behavior they describe.
Participant names, contact details, consent records, calibration, or study data enter Git or GitHub.
De-identified participant IDs are treated as research data and kept out of the public repository.
Raw study data is append-only; reruns use a unique suffix and preserve prior output.
Only synthetic fixtures approved for public disclosure may be committed.
Logs record application, commit, schema, config, scenario, session, and timing provenance.
Backups include per-session checksums and follow IRB and institutional retention rules.
Study operation sends telemetry or research data to unapproved cloud services.
Analysis preserves raw data, performs version-aware ingest, and records migrations.
The first data-collection release is tagged study-v1.0 after G8 passes.
Study config, rig calibration, scenarios, and sessions are frozen by recorded hashes; local.json is excluded.
A data-collection change creates a new tag and a study-log entry.
The release archive includes checksum manifest, build-info, licenses, operator docs, and diagnostics.
Release creation requires human approval and cannot substitute CI for hardware gate evidence.

Work Items.Title: Logging pipeline
Work Items.Action and substeps:
As specified in §6.4 and Appendix B:
Lock-free single-producer/single-consumer ring buffer of fixed-size sample structs (no allocation per sample). Sequence number on every sample; the consumer detects gaps and writes a SampleDropped event with the count.
Writer thread flushes to CSV every N ms (config, default 250 ms) using a pre-sized StringBuilder; fsync at block end.
Three streams per block: samples.csv (250 Hz), targets.csv (once per rendered frame, one row per active target), events.csv. One session.json per participant.
Every file starts with a #-prefixed header block: app version, git hash, config hashes, participant ID, block index, condition, order position, UTC at clock start, coordinate convention, schema version.
Directory layout: data/P{id}/block{n}_{cond}/…. Never overwrite: if a path exists, append a _r{k} suffix and log a RerunDetected event.
Work Items.Entry Criteria: G1 passed, or G0 with synthetic tracking
Work Items.Completion Evidence: 30-minute soak with the synthetic source at 250 Hz shows zero drops, files parse with the ingest script (P2.8), and the file sizes are as predicted.
Work Items.Validation: 30-minute soak with the synthetic source at 250 Hz shows zero drops, files parse with the ingest script (P2.8), and the file sizes are as predicted.

Risks.Risk: ELTS emission degrades Lighthouse tracking in WE blocks
Risks.Effect: Loses exactly the data that matters
Risks.Mitigation: White phosphor COB LEDs emit negligibly above 750 nm (§8); bench test at full intensity

Risks.Risk: Brio's Windows Hello IR illuminator is active under the Jetson pipeline
Risks.Mitigation: Confirm the IR stream is not opened; include the Brio in the IR test

Risks.Risk: ELTS light spills onto the display (washout)
Risks.Mitigation: Placement geometry (D-02); measured luminance on/off; aim limits on the ELTS if needed

Risks.Risk: Single-station occlusion
Risks.Mitigation: Log validity flags; exclude, never interpolate; characterize rate; adjust station placement

Risks.Risk: Head tracking error / mount shift makes the scene swim
Risks.Mitigation: Rigid non-stretch headband; rigidity test; corner rods; small rendering-only prediction

Risks.Risk: Tracking universe origin moves between sessions
Risks.Mitigation: RawAndUncalibrated universe; daily bore-laser check; corner rods

Risks.Risk: Trackers swap roles between sessions
Risks.Mitigation: Serial-number binding; startup self-check shows which serial is which

Risks.Risk: Trigger reads false (role not held-in-hand)
Risks.Mitigation: Role set in SteamVR; self-check requires one trigger press before a session

Risks.Risk: Pose prediction contaminates the DV
Risks.Mitigation: 0 s prediction on the tracking thread; rendering prediction never enters the log

Risks.Risk: Two clocks (Unity, Jetson) drift
Risks.Effect: ELTS on/off misaligned with aim data
Risks.Mitigation: Ack timestamps and offset estimation per command; heartbeat; Jetson event log

Risks.Risk: LEDs stay on after a software failure
Risks.Mitigation: Heartbeat timeout; max on-time guard; physical E-stop

Risks.Risk: Dropped samples under load
Risks.Mitigation: Lock-free ring buffer; sequence numbers; drop counter on the operator panel; soak tests

Risks.Risk: Operator view appears on the participant display
Risks.Mitigation: Fixed display assignment in config; identification splash; refusal with < 2 displays

Risks.Risk: Frame hitches on the stimulus display
Risks.Mitigation: Light scene; profiling; FrameHitch events logged

Risks.Risk: Data loss (crash, power)
Risks.Mitigation: Per-block files; 250 ms flush; fsync at block end; nightly backup with checksums

Risks.Risk: Headband incompatible with eye tracker or IMU
Risks.Mitigation: Early compatibility fit with the real devices

Risks.Risk: Scope creep from "modular for future studies"
Risks.Mitigation: The extension points in §12.5 are the modularity; anything beyond them is deferred past study-v1.0

Risks.Risk: Registration error with scale/skew components (does not cancel within-subjects)
Risks.Mitigation: Corner-probe tolerances on the lengths of U and V and on their angle; prioritize corner spacing over absolute position (§5.5)

Risks.Risk: Realistic replica on campus
Risks.Mitigation: Bright color, label, locked storage, written notice

Risks.Risk: Procurement lead time
Risks.Mitigation: Order on day 1; Phase 2 proceeds on synthetic poses

Risks.Risk: Participant trips or bumps equipment while moving
Risks.Mitigation: Clear standing zone; cable-free participant (trackers are wireless); daily rig check

Risks.Risk: Agent or workbook status diverges from repository state
Risks.Effect: The team acts on stale progress
Risks.Mitigation: Append-only progress events, deterministic reducer, CI regeneration check; JSON state overrides workbook status

Risks.Risk: Two agents edit the same task or files concurrently
Risks.Mitigation: One owner and branch per task; declared path claims; separate worktrees; reducer rejects divergent task event chains

Risks.Risk: Toolchain or dependency drift across machines
Risks.Effect: Builds or analyses cannot be reproduced
Risks.Mitigation: Exact versions, lockfiles, doctor reports, clean-machine portability tests

Risks.Risk: Secrets, hardware identifiers, or research data enter the public repository
Risks.Mitigation: Templates only, deny patterns, secret/data scans, human review, private deployment overlays where required

Risks.Risk: An AI-generated change alters a scientific invariant or safety control
Risks.Effect: Invalid study data or unsafe operation
Risks.Mitigation: Invariant tests, protected paths, human approval, gate re-verification

taskDefinitions.title: Tracking service

source.Title: Tracking service
source.Action and substeps:
Productionize the P1.5–P1.9 spikes into TrackingService:
Dedicated thread, 250 Hz (rate in config), polling pose + controller state for both bound devices with 0 s prediction in the universe chosen at P1.7.
Handedness conversion applied exactly once, here.
Per device: position, quaternion, valid, connected, trackingResult, and for WEAPON the trigger state.
Trigger edge detector: on falling edge, record Clock.Now as the shot time, emit a Shot request, lock out further edges for 20 ms (config).
Publishes the latest sample to the main thread through a lock-free double buffer; publishes every sample to the logging ring buffer.
Separate optional "rendering head pose" with configurable small prediction (default 0 s until tuned in P3.6); never enters the log.
Rebinding on device activate/deactivate events; a device that is not bound reports connected = false.

taskDefinitions.title: Logging pipeline

source.Title: Logging pipeline
source.Action and substeps:
As specified in §6.4 and Appendix B:
Lock-free single-producer/single-consumer ring buffer of fixed-size sample structs (no allocation per sample). Sequence number on every sample; the consumer detects gaps and writes a SampleDropped event with the count.
Writer thread flushes to CSV every N ms (config, default 250 ms) using a pre-sized StringBuilder; fsync at block end.
Three streams per block: samples.csv (250 Hz), targets.csv (once per rendered frame, one row per active target), events.csv. One session.json per participant.
Every file starts with a #-prefixed header block: app version, git hash, config hashes, participant ID, block index, condition, order position, UTC at clock start, coordinate convention, schema version.
Directory layout: data/P{id}/block{n}_{cond}/…. Never overwrite: if a path exists, append a _r{k} suffix and log a RerunDetected event.
source.Entry Criteria: G1 passed, or G0 with synthetic tracking
source.Completion Evidence: 30-minute soak with the synthetic source at 250 Hz shows zero drops, files parse with the ingest script (P2.8), and the file sizes are as predicted.
source.Validation: 30-minute soak with the synthetic source at 250 Hz shows zero drops, files parse with the ingest script (P2.8), and the file sizes are as predicted.

taskDefinitions.title: Session state machine

source.Title: Session state machine
source.Action and substeps: States: Idle → SessionSetup → Calibration (Phase 5 fills this in) → Practice → for each block BlockReady → BlockRunning → BlockEnded → Break → … → SessionComplete. taskDefinitions.title: Fail-safes

source.Title: Fail-safes
source.Action and substeps:
Heartbeat timeout: if no PING for 3 s (config) in Active, inhibit LEDs and return to Armed; log it.
Max on-time guard: LEDs are hard-limited to block duration + 30 s per START (the duration_s field of the START message) (config; must be consistent with the exposure limits in the safety sheet, D-13).
Physical E-stop: a normally-closed switch in the LED supply path (or at the transistor gate) that the operator can hit regardless of software state. Existing hardware is modified only at this one point, and the ELTS otherwise remains as evaluated.
